'''Orazio Svelto''' (21 February 1936 – 10 January 2026) was an Italian physicist, academic and author. He was an Emeritus Professor of Physics at [[Politecnico di Milano]].<ref name=aes>{{Cite web|url=https://www.polimi.it/en/il-politecnico/storia-dellateneo/professors-emeriti-and-honorary/orazio-svelto|title=Orazio Svelto - polimi|website=www.polimi.it}}</ref>
 
Svelto explored a range of topics in [[Laser science|Laser Physics]] and [[Photonics]] over the years, notably areas like [[Ultrashort pulse|ultrashort-pulse]] generation, laser resonator physics, and [[solid-state lasers]]. His notable contributions to the field also include the invention of the hollow fiber (now often referred to as the Hollow Capillary Fiber, HCF) compressor of optical pulses.<ref name=lzx>{{Cite journal|url=https://pubs.aip.org/aip/apl/article-abstract/68/20/2793/521166/Generation-of-high-energy-10-fs-pulses-by-a-new?redirectedFrom=fulltext|title=Generation of high energy 10 fs pulses by a new pulse compression technique|first1=M.|last1=Nisoli|first2=S.|last2=De Silvestri|first3=O.|last3=Svelto|date=May 13, 1996|journal=Applied Physics Letters|volume=68|issue=20|pages=2793–2795|via=Silverchair|doi=10.1063/1.116609|bibcode=1996ApPhL..68.2793N |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His scholarly publications include scientific papers published in journals, such as ''[[Physical Review Letters|Phys Rev. Letters]]'', ''[[Applied Physics Letters]]'', and ''[[Optics Letters]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZntbwtYAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Orazio Svelto|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> Additionally, he has authored and co-authored books, including ''Problems in Laser Physics'' and ''Principles of Lasers'', which has progressed to its fifth edition and has been translated into multiple languages.<ref name=bes>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00107514.2011.647714|title=Principles of Lasers, 5th edn., by O. Svelto: Scope: monograph. Level: advanced undergraduate and above|first=Manuel|last=Vogel|date=March 1, 2012|journal=Contemporary Physics|volume=53|issue=2|pages=173|via=Taylor and Francis+NEJM|doi=10.1080/00107514.2011.647714|bibcode=2012ConPh..53..173V |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
 
Svelto served as a Vice-President of the Italian Association for Electronics and as a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]]. Moreover, he has received awards, including the Quantum Electronics Prize,<ref name=ces>{{Cite web|url=https://qeod.epsdivisions.org/eps-qeod-quantum-electronics-and-optics-prize/|title=EPS-QEOD Quantum Electronics and Optics Prize – EPS Quantum Electronics and Optics Division (QEOD)|website=qeod.epsdivisions.org}}</ref> the Italgas Prize,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/History/Biographies/bios/Orazio_Svelto|title=Orazio Svelto &#124; Optica|website=www.optica.org}}</ref> the Gold Medal of the President of the Italian Republic for deserving citizens in Science, Culture, and Art,<ref name=tzx>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quirinale.it/onorificenze/insigniti/161484|title=Le onorificenze della Repubblica Italiana|website=www.quirinale.it}}</ref> the Charles Hard Townes Medal,<ref name=jes>{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/awards/award_descriptions/charlestownes/|title=Charles Hard Townes Medal &#124; Optica|website=www.optica.org}}</ref> and the Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/340/updates/17188340|title=Applied Physics B|website=SpringerLink}}</ref><ref name=kzx>{{Cite web|url=https://www.electrooptics.com/news/orazio-svelto-receives-julius-springer-prize-applied-physics-2011|title=Orazio Svelto receives Julius Springer Prize for Applied Physics 2011 &#124; Electro Optics|website=www.electrooptics.com}}</ref>

==Background==
Svelto earned a degree in [[Nuclear Engineering]] from Politecnico di Milano in 1960. From 1961 to 1963, he was a [[Research Associate]] at the Microwave Laboratory at [[Stanford University]], supported by a fellowship from the [[National Research Council (Italy)|Italian National Research Council (CNR)]]. Between 1963 and 1976, he held various positions at CNR, including Researcher, Head of Research, and Research Director. In 1966, he received the "Libera Docenza" degree in Quantum Electronics, which was reaffirmed in 1972. From 1976 to 2010, he was a Full Professor of Quantum Electronics and Physics of Matter at Politecnico di Milano and has held the title of Emeritus Professor since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fisi.polimi.it/en/staff/orazio.svelto|title=Svelto Orazio|website=Department of Physics}}</ref> Moreover, in 1976, he also established the Center for Quantum Electronics and Electronics Instrumentation, which he directed until 2000 when it merged with the Institute for Photonics and Nanotechnologies at CNR.<ref name=aes/>

Svelto died in Milan on 10 January 2026, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |title=Addio a Orazio Svelto, pioniere della ricerca sui laser in Italia |url=https://www.laprovinciaunicatv.it/stories/premium/ansa-tecnologia/addio-a-orazio-svelto-pioniere-della-ricerca-sui-laser-in-italia-o_3575531_11/ |access-date=10 January 2026 |publisher=La Provincia Unica |date=10 January 2026}}</ref>

==Works==
In 1988, Svelto and his coworkers invented the super-Gaussian mirrors for [[solid-state laser]] with unstable [[resonators]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/240|title=Solid-state laser unstable resonators with tapered reflectivity mirrors: the super-Gaussian approach|first1=S.|last1=De Silvestri|first2=P.|last2=Laporta|first3=V.|last3=Magni|first4=O.|last4=Svelto|date=June 7, 1988|journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics|volume=24|issue=6|pages=1172–1177|via=IEEE Xplore|doi=10.1109/3.240|bibcode=1988IJQE...24.1172D |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Another notable contribution to the field is the invention and development, in 1991, of an efficient diode-pumped continuous-wave Er:Yb:glass laser.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Diode-pumped cw bulk Er:Yb:glass laser|first1=P.|last1=Laporta|first2=S.|last2=De Silvestri|first3=V.|last3=Magni|first4=O.|last4=Svelto|date=December 15, 1991|journal=Optics Letters|volume=16|issue=24|pages=1952–1954|doi=10.1364/ol.16.001952|pmid=19784192 |bibcode=1991OptL...16.1952L }}</ref> Later in 1996, in a collaborative study, he and his coworkers invented an optical compression technique, generating 10 fs pulses with 240 μJ energy via hollow-core waveguide broadening and prism-based compression.<ref name=lzx/> By advancing this, he compressed high-energy laser pulses below 5 fs using spectral broadening in a hollow fiber and dispersion compensation.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://opg.optica.org/ol/abstract.cfm?uri=ol-22-8-522|title=Compression of high-energy laser pulses below 5 fs|first1=M.|last1=Nisoli|first2=S. De|last2=Silvestri|first3=O.|last3=Svelto|first4=R.|last4=Szipöcs|first5=K.|last5=Ferencz|first6=Ch|last6=Spielmann|first7=S.|last7=Sartania|first8=F.|last8=Krausz|date=April 15, 1997|journal=Optics Letters|volume=22|issue=8|pages=522–524|via=opg.optica.org|doi=10.1364/OL.22.000522|pmid=18183254 |bibcode=1997OptL...22..522N |url-access=subscription}}</ref> In the same year, he achieved multigigawatt sub-5-fs pulse generation using a novel high-energy compression system, optimizing spectral broadening and dispersion control for unprecedented pulse shortening to 4.5 fs.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Nisoli |first1=M. |last2=Stagira |first2=S. |last3=De Silvestri |first3=S. |last4=Svelto |first4=O. |last5=Sartania |first5=S. |last6=Cheng |first6=Z. |last7=Lenzner |first7=M. |last8=Spielmann |first8=C. |last9=Krausz |first9=F. |title=A novel-high energy pulse compression system: generation of multigigawatt sub-5-fs pulses |journal=Applied Physics B: Lasers and Optics |date=1997 |volume=65 |issue=2 |pages=189–196 |doi=10.1007/s003400050263 |bibcode=1997ApPhB..65..189N |s2cid=119807055 }}</ref> 
 
Svelto authored and co-authored several books, including ''Principles of Lasers'', which provides an overview of laser physics, technology, behavior, and applications. In its fourth edition, the book was reviewed in the journal ''Sensor Review'', where it was described as "well presented and clearly explained."<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/sr.1999.19.4.325.2/full/html|title=Principles of Lasers 4th edition|first1=O.|last1=Svelto|first2=D.C.|last2=Hanna|date=January 1, 1999|journal=Sensor Review|volume=19|issue=4|pages=325–326|via=Emerald Insight|doi=10.1108/sr.1999.19.4.325.2|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The fifth edition of ''Principles of Lasers'' also aimed to provide an explanation of laser behavior, covering its principles, schemes, and technologies, along with practical examples.<ref name=bes/> Moreover, his other multi-edition book, ''Problems in Laser Physics'', addressed laser physics problems, including radiation interaction, wave propagation, pumping, laser behavior, and beam transformation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://squ.on.worldcat.org/search?queryString=no%3A840283736|title=Problems in Laser Physics}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*1990 – Elected Member, [[Accademia Nazionale delle Scienze detta dei XL]]
*1991 – G. Borgia Foundation Prize, Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei
*1993 – Elected Fellow, [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]]
*1998 – Quantum Electronics Prize, [[European Physical Society]]<ref name=ces/>
*1999 – Sergio Panizza, [[Italian Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sif.it/attivita/altri_premi/bando_panizza_galimberti/vincitori|title=Vincitori e vincitrici Premio per l'Optoelettronica e la Fotonica "Sergio Panizza e Gabriele Galimberti"|website=www.sif.it}}</ref>
*1999 – Elected Fellow, [[Optica (society)|Optical Society of America (OSA)]]
*2000 – ITALGAS Prize, Italgas
*2004 – Elected Member, [[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lincei.it/en/soci/classe-di-scienze-fisiche?field_soci_qualifica_value_i18n=All&field_soci_cognome_ordine_value=Svelto|title=Physical Sciences Class–Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Soci Nazionali |url=https://www.accademiaxl.it/accademia/soci/soci-nazionali/ |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=www.accademiaxl.it |language=it-IT}}</ref>
*2005 – Gold medal, The Presidency of the Republic<ref name=tzx/>
*2006 – Charles Hard Townes Medal, Optica, with the following motivation: "For pioneering works on ultrashort laser pulses and solid state lasers and for the invention of the hollow-fiber compressor leading to advances in extreme nonlinear optics and attosecond science"<ref name=jes/>
*2006–2012 – Member of the Scientific Advisory Board, [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]] ([[Erlangen]], Germany)
*2011 – [[Julius Springer]] Prize, ''[[Springer Publishing|Springer]]'', with the following motivation: "For his pioneering, long lasting, and innovative work in the fields of lasers and optics. He is an internationally renowned laser and photonics scientist and one of the worldwide leaders of the scientific community in this field"<ref name=kzx/><ref name="auto"/>
